title: LifeTox: Unveiling Implicit Toxicity in Life Advice
authors: Minbeom Kim, Jahyun Koo, Hwanhee Lee, Joonsuk Park, Hwaran Lee, Kyomin Jung
text:
As large language models (LLMs) continue to be integrated into our daily lives, ensuring their safety is becoming increasingly crucial [1,2,3]. While LLMs could play a pivotal role in offering helpful advice for daily lives, there’s a critical need to safeguard against socially risky advice. However, existing safety benchmarks and red teaming prompts [4,5] often fail to capture the implicit toxicity in complex real-life advice-seeking scenarios. This results in a gap where the nuanced and context-specific risks inherent in LLM responses are not adequately addressed [6,7,8].

To bridge this gap, we introduce LifeTox, a dataset of 87,510 real-life scenarios and respective advice crawled from two twin subreddit forums: LifeProTips (LPT) and UnethicalLifeProTips (ULPT). These platforms serve as venues for users to discuss problems in their personal lives and request helpful tips. Strict guidelines dictate that LPT is reserved for exchanging ethical living tips, whereas ULPT permits unethical advice only, as illustrated in Figure 1. Leveraging these subreddits, LifeTox is designed to capture implicit toxicity in advice for various personal advice-seeking contexts, thereby facilitating the training of robust and generalizable toxicity detectors.

LifeTox distinctively stands out from previous safety benchmarks with its unique features. First, it integrates questions that vividly describe detailed personal experiences, thereby providing a long and in-depth context for the advice sought. This is demonstrated by the extensive average length of the questions and the breadth of vocabulary, as shown in Table 1. Second, LifeTox -trained models probes into implicit toxicity [9,4] —more subtle aspect of whether the advice promotes socially inappropriate or harmful behaviors, independent of explicit profanity uses. Such focus on the underlying intent and societal impact of the advice differentiates LifeTox from existing works; This ensures that toxicity detection is not just based on surface-level indicators but also the deeper social implications of the advice. Consequently, LifeTox offers a thorough approach to understanding and detecting implicit toxicity, grounded in the societal context and the real-life complexity of personal experiences.

Our experiments show LifeTox ’s effectiveness for training generalizable toxicity classifiers. RoBERTa [10] fine-tuned on LifeTox demonstrates strong generalization capability across various out-of-domain safety benchmarks such as HHH Alignments [11], HarmfulQ [12], and BeaverTails [13]. It matches or exceeds the zero-shot results of large language models (>7B). It also exhibits superior performance on unseen benchmarks. Even, LifeTox fine-tuning also enhances large language models for zero-shot toxicity classifications. This validates the significance of LifeTox as a resource for better addressing implicit toxicity in real-life advice-seeking scenarios.
